turns.customer: Honestly, why should I use you instead of a Rover sitter or that other kennel on 183? Which is better?
blocks:
Fair question. I can’t say Happy Tails is better than a Rover sitter or the kennel on 183 without knowing which sitter or kennel you mean and comparing their actual offerings. I can help you compare them against your priorities.

Happy Tails’ published boarding details include indoor/outdoor suites, raised beds and fresh bedding, twice-daily cleaning, morning and afternoon potty walks, and group or individual play as safety permits. Luxury suites add features such as a live webcam, TV, and extra play. Rates are **$65/day for Standard**, **$90/day for Luxury**, and **$85/day for Tiny Town** for dogs 25 lb and under. Reservations are required.

A useful comparison is total cost and billing rules, overnight supervision, exercise and play options, updates or cameras, medication and feeding needs, cancellation terms, and how well the setup fits Pip’s routine and temperament. Happy Tails requires current vaccination documentation for boarding. Its published cancellation terms are at least 24 hours’ notice for non-holiday dog boarding; holiday stays have separate deposit and five-day cancellation terms.

If you share the other kennel’s name or a link—and what matters most to you—I can help make a side-by-side comparison. I can also suggest questions to ask a Rover sitter.

turns.customer: Fine. What do I actually get with your luxury suite?
